note.question: How can a data intermediary obtain informed consent, truthfully elicit private privacy costs, and sell representative individual-level samples without paying the prohibitive cost of uniform high compensation?
note.overview: Data subjects privately value privacy and can strategically report that value. The proposed second-compensation procurement auction is individually rational and incentive compatible, and is embedded in a sampling mechanism that purchases an unbiased data sample.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The platform maintains qualifying data subjects and their sensitive attributes. A buyer requests a sample of size n for specified quasi-identifiers. The platform announces the mechanism, elicits reported privacy concerns, orders subjects by the sensitive attribute, repeatedly samples adjacent rolling pairs, buys the lower-reported-cost record in each pair, pays the other record's privacy cost, and delivers the anonymized sample to the buyer. Each pair functions as a reverse second-price auction for one record.
